doc.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
doc.interviewee: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor

title: Hearing the Original Creole Band and Bill Johnson
summary: Taylor recalls first hearing the Creole band about 1914 on its tour, backing an entertainer, with Bill Johnson and Keppard.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did you hear him with the original Creole, the Bill Johnson's band? And they're on the stage?
No, I'm not gonna say... They played the first time I heard that. I never... That was... They had a fella... Entertainer. Who was his band. I'm quite sure. H.M. Prince.
I think was the fella. Yeah.

It was his band. And he did a song and dance or something. And this band backed him up. And I know they came... know they were since then they came into St. York. I was waiting to the Brook of Washington. And we could hear the Creole there in downtown. I don't think I did how to hear them. I don't think I did. But I think I heard them in a different, some other place.
Was that their tour about 1915 or 16? Yeah.
That was, you see, I was first at St. Louis was 13. 14. This was around 14. Oh, come on. Creole band.
Everybody knew that they had something there, huh? Oh, yeah. In downtown DeHern.
Maybe Vinson was in that band. This band? No, that was the Creole band that you're talking about. Because he and Kepard knew each other well. They worked together. Yeah.
Yeah, Bill Johnson was kind of random. There was men here in the group. Yeah. All the theory, I think.
Yeah. There was a bandit player, I think, since then. Here, Omar. He had a little here, Little Mitch. There was men driving.
